title: ag-ui-protocol/ag-ui — AG-UI: the Agent-User Interaction Protocol. Bring Agents into Frontend Applications.
content:
AG-UI is an open, lightweight, event-based protocol that standardizes how AI agents connect to user-facing applications. Built for simplicity and flexibility, it enables seamless integration between AI agents, real time user context, and user interfaces.
Join our Discord → Read the Docs → Go to the AG-UI Dojo → Follow us →
Create a new AG-UI application in seconds:
npx create-ag-ui-app my-agent-app
AG-UI is an open, lightweight, event-based protocol for agent-human interaction, designed for simplicity & flexibility:
- During agent executions, agent backends emit events compatible with one of AG-UI's ~16 standard event types
- Agent backends can accept one of a few simple AG-UI compatible inputs as arguments
AG-UI includes a flexible middleware layer that ensures compatibility across diverse environments:
- Works with any event transport (SSE, WebSockets, webhooks, etc.)
- Allows for loose event format matching, enabling broad agent and app interoperability
It also ships with a reference HTTP implementation and default connector to help teams get started fast.
AG-UI was developed based on real-world requirements and practical experience building in-app agent interactions.
AG-UI is complementary to the other 2 top agentic protocols
- MCP gives agents tools
- A2A allows agents to communicate with other agents
- AG-UI brings agents into user-facing applications
- 💬 Real-time agentic chat with streaming
- 🔄 Bi-directional state synchronization
- 🧩 Generative UI and structured messages
- 🧠 Real-time context enrichment
- 🛠️ Frontend tool integration
- 🧑💻 Human-in-the-loop collaboration
AG-UI was born from CopilotKit's initial partnership with LangChain and CrewAI - and brings the incredibly popular agent-user-interactivity infrastructure to the wider agentic ecosystem.

report.summary: AG-UI is an open, event-based protocol that standardizes how AI agents connect to user-facing applications, complementing MCP and A2A.
report.background: As AI agents move from demos to production, the ecosystem has split into specialized layers: MCP for tool access and A2A for agent-to-agent collaboration, but no standard for agent-to-user interfaces. Teams often build custom WebSocket or SSE bridges, leading to duplicated work and poor interoperability. AG-UI emerged from CopilotKit's work with LangChain and CrewAI to fill that gap. It defines a lightweight event-based contract between agent backends and frontends, so agents can stream state, request frontend tools, and collaborate with humans. By aligning with existing transports and offering reference implementations, it aims to become the missing user-interaction layer in the emerging agent protocol stack.
key_points: AG-UI defines roughly 16 standard event types for agent execution. Agent backends emit these events and accept simple AG-UI-compatible inputs, creating a consistent contract between agents and user-facing apps. This reduces custom glue code and lets frontends react to streaming updates, tool calls, and state changes predictably.

It includes a flexible middleware layer that is transport-agnostic, working over SSE, WebSockets, webhooks and more. Loose event format matching allows broad interoperability, while a reference HTTP implementation and default connector help teams get started quickly.

AG-UI is positioned as complementary to MCP and A2A. MCP gives agents tools, A2A lets agents talk to other agents, and AG-UI brings agents into user-facing applications. Together they cover tools, agent collaboration, and human interaction.

Core capabilities include real-time streaming chat, bi-directional state synchronization, generative UI and structured messages, real-time context enrichment, frontend tool integration, and human-in-the-loop collaboration. These features target production in-app agent experiences rather than standalone chatbots.

Developers can scaffold a project with npx create-ag-ui-app. The AG-UI Dojo demonstrates core building blocks in 50-200 lines per example, with framework integrations and source code available. The project is MIT licensed and has a public roadmap and biweekly working group.
report.impact: For the AI industry, AG-UI could become the frontend standard in the agent protocol stack, reducing fragmentation and accelerating agent adoption. It strengthens the MCP/A2A ecosystem by adding the missing user-interaction layer, and may push frameworks to support it natively. For developers, it means less custom plumbing, faster prototyping, and reusable UI patterns, though they must learn event-driven contracts and choose transports. For regular users, it promises more responsive, context-aware AI apps with streaming answers, generative interfaces, and meaningful human oversight. Adoption will depend on ecosystem buy-in beyond CopilotKit, LangChain, and CrewAI, but the open MIT license and reference implementations lower the barrier.
report.tools: Follow the AG-UI GitHub repo, create-ag-ui-app, and AG-UI Dojo for hands-on examples. Related protocols: MCP for tools and A2A for agent-to-agent communication. Framework integrations include CopilotKit, LangChain, and CrewAI. Watch for SSE/WebSocket transports and the reference HTTP connector. These let you test agent-frontend streaming, state sync, and human-in-the-loop patterns.
